country.comment: The study analyzes state water supply and sanitation company privatization (via stock-market IPO) in Brazil, focusing empirically on the state of Minas Gerais (COPASA) alongside national Brazilian PNSB comparisons.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Section 'The context and the study at hand'; PDF p. 3; PDF p. 4, Section 'Methodology'

effect_estimate.comment: Tables 1-12 and Figures 1-8 were embedded as rasterized images in the source PDF so cell-level point estimates and p-values inside tables/figures are not present in the extracted text stream; all sample counts, confidence thresholds (95%), and directional statistical test outcomes reported in the prose are extracted verbatim/faithfully.
effect_estimate.value: In 10-year municipal comparisons in Minas Gerais (64 municipalities managed throughout 2000-2010 by COPASA vs. 256 managed by municipal organizations; Mann-Whitney U test at 95% confidence), COPASA's 2006 stock-market IPO did not produce superior access outcomes: COPASA-exclusively served municipalities experienced a slight setback in household water access (2000-2008), significantly poorer progress in increasing households supplied by the general water network (Figure 3), significantly lower progress in reducing the share of households without a bathroom or WC (Figure 6), and no statistically significant difference in household bathroom/WC presence (Figure 4) or connection to the general sewage/rainwater network (Figure 5). Prior to post-2009 regulatory agency oversight, annual tariff readjustments unilaterally set by COPASA almost always exceeded official inflation indices (INPC/IPCA), while user complaints and court actions increased continuously and the share of resolved complaints declined (exact numeric cell values in Tables 1-12 and Figures 1-8 were rasterized in the PDF and not printed in prose).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF pp. 8-14, Section 'Advancements and perspectives in COPASA's management: for what reason and for whom?' and Section 'Conclusions'

mechanism_certainty.comment: Rated 2 (mechanism directly observed), respecting the <=2 ceiling for mixed-methods (MMAT) designs. Through 15 insider/regulator interviews, legislation, and COPASA/IBGE administrative records, the study directly documents how post-IPO profitability and capital-return rules blocked concessions in small/poor/rural areas and sewage expansion, how manager bonus targets drove municipal concession expansion, how unilateral above-inflation tariff hikes operated before post-2009 regulatory oversight, and how outsourcing and rising unresolved complaints affected service waiting times.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 6-13, Section 'Advancements and perspectives in COPASA's management: for what reason and for whom?'

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines selective concession expansion excluding small municipalities, poor areas, and rural sanitation due to profitability thresholds (ELIGIBILITY: service_area); unilateral above-inflation tariff readjustments passed to users and longer service/repair waiting times from outsourcing (BURDEN: fees, delay); lack of tariff malleability/flexibility for poorer users (DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION: accommodation); and rising Customer Service/consumer-protection complaints, court actions, declining complaint resolution, post-2009 ARSAE regulatory oversight, and federal-state-municipal policy coordination (ENFORCEMENT: complaint, judicial_review, political_coordination).
mechanism_flags.value: ELIGIBILITY, BURDEN, DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, ENFORCEMENT, service_area, fees, delay, accommodation, complaint, judicial_review, political_coordination
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 6-13, Section 'Advancements and perspectives in COPASA's management: for what reason and for whom?'

outcome_flags.comment: Analyzes household general water and sewage network connections (formal_connection), forms of household water supply and bathroom/septic-tank sanitation access (water_access, sanitation_access), municipal water and sanitation coverage rates (service_coverage), water treatment and water quality standards compliance (service_quality), interview evidence on supply regularity/interruptions/intermittence/rationing (service_continuity), tariff hikes relative to inflation and expense for low-income users (affordability), and longer waiting times for service provision and repairs (delay).
outcome_flags.value: formal_connection, water_access, sanitation_access, service_coverage, service_quality, service_continuity, affordability, delay

sample_size.comment: Also analyzes COPASA annual reports/financial statements for 2003-2012 and national paired state/municipal PNSB samples (2000 and 2008) for Brazil as a whole (exact national N in Figures 1-2 not printed in prose because table/figure graphics were rasterized).
sample_size.value: 320 municipalities in Minas Gerais in main longitudinal comparison (64 municipalities served throughout 2000-2010 by COPASA and 256 by municipal organizations; drawn from broader cross-sections of 67 and 128 COPASA municipalities and 346 and 284 municipal-organization municipalities in 2000 and 2008/2010); 15 semi-structured interviews with specialists, managers, and technicians

study_design.comment: Integrates secondary quantitative longitudinal/comparative municipal and company indicator analysis (2000-2010 / 2003-2012) with primary qualitative interviews and document/legal review.
study_design.value: Mixed-methods comparative case study combining quantitative descriptive and non-parametric inferential analysis of official municipal and utility panel data (Wilcoxon paired test and Mann-Whitney U test on 2000-2010 indicator changes) with document/legislation analysis and 15 semi-structured interviews (content and discourse analysis)
